title: Commutative group space and smooth integral-fibre hypotheses
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $G$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A commutative group structure is a commutative group structure on $G(T)$ for every $S$-scheme $T$, with restriction maps preserving multiplication and the identity. Thus multiplication, inverse and identity are natural and define group algebraic-space operations. The identity section $e:S\to G$ sends every test point to the group identity. Write $\overline S=h_S$ for the represented base space, $p:G\to\overline S$ for its unique structure morphism, and use Yoneda for maps between represented spaces [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Define $G\to S$ to be smooth, separated and of finite presentation with geometrically integral fibres as follows: smoothness and local finite presentation are the chart tests [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] with scheme smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and local finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; the relative diagonal is representable by closed immersions; $p$ and its diagonal are quasi-compact in the affine-scheme-test sense [def-sfb-proper-curve-moduli]. For every algebraically closed field $K$ in the scheme universe and every $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, the sheaf fibre product with $G$ has an irreducible point space with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and every representable etale scheme chart of that fibre is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The latter two conditions say exactly that the geometric fibre is integral. None of these conditions assumes that $G$ is a scheme.
